summary: Cross-site scripting through link titles when html is enabled
details: When the html option is true, lanternmd copied the title of a Markdown link into the title attribute without escaping quotes. Input such as [x](https://a.example "a" onmouseover="alert(1)") produced an extra attribute. Rendering with html: false (the default) escapes titles and is not affected.

affectedWhen: the Markdown comes from people you do not trust
notAffectedWhen: html is false or unset (the default)
the rendered HTML goes through a sanitizer such as DOMPurify before it reaches a page
only your own authors write the Markdown
desk.vexHint: not_affected with vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path when html is off; inline_mitigations_already_exist when output is sanitized
